skills: Year 1
Chemistry foundations you can use: structures, functional groups, equilibria, units.
Laboratory discipline: weighing, volumetric work, a notebook, a clean bench.
Anatomy and physiology as systems you can sketch.
Pharmaceutical calculations: ratios, percentages, dilutions, molarity.
Year 2
Dosage forms and what each excipient is doing in them.
Analytical basics: titrations, spectrophotometry, calibration curves, error.
Microbiology technique: aseptic handling, culture, sterilisation.
Biochemistry and pharmacognosy summarised on your own sheets.
Year 3
Pharmacology by drug class: mechanism, uses, adverse effects, interactions - on cards you wrote.
Medicinal chemistry: structure-activity relationships you can draw.
Pharmaceutical technology: unit operations and in-process quality control tests.
Clinical and hospital pharmacy: reading a prescription, counselling a patient.
Year 4
Quality systems vocabulary: GMP, SOP, validation, documentation.
Instrumental analysis: what HPLC, UV-Visible, FTIR and GC each tell you.
Biopharmaceutics and pharmacokinetics calculations done fluently.
In-plant training notes turned into interview answers; a research project you can explain in two minutes.
dept.career_intro: The department's career page describes where pharmacy graduates go: the pharmaceutical industry, government bodies, hospitals, model pharmacies, teaching and research. The table follows that page; the right-hand column is general advice, not an EWU rule.
careers: Production
Running manufacturing lines for tablets, capsules, liquids, injectables and more.
Pharmaceutical technology courses, in-plant training in a production department, GMP vocabulary.
Quality control and quality assurance
Testing raw materials and finished products; guarding the documentation and the system.
Pharmaceutical analysis courses, instrument cards, attention to documentation.
Research and development
Formulating new products and improving old ones.
Pharmaceutics, biopharmaceutics, a formulation-flavoured project.
Regulatory affairs
Preparing the dossiers and submissions that keep products on the market.
Pharmacy law and ethics, careful writing, knowing what the drug regulator asks for.
Marketing and sales
Product management and medical promotion.
Pharmacology you can explain simply, pharmaceutical management and marketing, presentation practice.
Supply chain
Planning, procurement and distribution of medicines.
Spreadsheets, pharmaceutical management, interest in how a plant actually runs.
Government service
The career page names drug-regulation posts (Superintendent of Drugs, Drug Inspector) and research posts at BCSIR.
Recruitment-examination preparation, pharmacy law, analysis.
Hospital and model pharmacy
Patient-facing practice. The career page notes that a Level I model pharmacy must be run by an A-grade pharmacist.
Clinical and hospital pharmacy, counselling practice, professional registration.
Teaching, research and higher study
Faculty positions for top graduates; master's and PhD study at home or abroad.
CGPA, a research project, test scores, recommenders.
career_notes: Pharmacy practice in Bangladesh is regulated by the Pharmacy Council of Bangladesh (PCB). EWU requires newly admitted B.Pharm students to complete online pre-registration with the PCB, through the department, within the first three months of their first semester - if you are new, do this first.
The steps from graduation to registration as a pharmacist are set by the PCB and have changed over the years. Ask the department office and check the Council's current notices in your final year.

book.title: The B.Pharm Degree Planner
book.subtitle: Department of Pharmacy, East West University
lines: Thirty-nine PHRM courses, two long semesters a year and one professional register at the end. A planner built around drug cards, lab records, calculations and the road into industry.
small: Curriculum, rules, fees and dates checked against East West University's official web pages on 10 October 2026.

Unofficial. An independent planner for students. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or issued by East West University. Always confirm requirements with your advisor, the student portal and official notices.

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole B.Pharm degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm) as EWU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on EWU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - EWU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official EWU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from EWU's own web pages on 10 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Your data

Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from East West University's published pages as they stood on 10 October 2026; the source is named under each section.
The grading scale
A+ to D are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA.
Three things students get wrong

items: **An F stays in the sum.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top, until you retake the course and the old F becomes an R.
**Heavier courses move the CGPA more.** A 4-credit course with a lab outweighs a 3-credit one. Protect the heavy courses first.
**W, I, P and S never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

book.text: Codes that are not letter grades

rows: Incomplete. Given only at the end of a semester when everything except the final exam is done; the instructor files an Incomplete Grade Form.
Finish within one week of the next semester's start (the calendar prints the 'last day to clear I grades'). After that it turns into an F, or into the tentative grade if one was assigned.
Withdrawal. You officially dropped the course before the calendar's withdrawal deadline. No credit, not in GPA.
Use it on purpose, not by accident: the deadline falls about two weeks before classes end.
A repeated course. An earlier attempt that a retake has replaced. No credit, not in GPA, still printed on the grade report.
Pass / Satisfactory. Counts toward graduation, not in GPA.

book.text: Source: EWU 'Grades, Rules and Regulations' page, ewubd.edu/grades-rules-and-regulations.
Retakes

items: You may retake a course **only once** to improve a grade you already earned.
An **F can be retaken as many times as it takes** to pass, inside the time limit for graduation. The earlier F becomes R.
Only your **most recent attempt** counts in GPA and CGPA. Every attempt stays on the grade report.
A retake needs the **Department Chair's written permission** and full tuition, lab and other fees.
Students who use the retake policy are **not eligible for the Gold Medal, awards or distinction**, and the scholarship rules list retaking courses among the things that make a student ineligible.

book.title: Before you retake a passing grade
items: Run the numbers in the CGPA tab's retake what-if. A B- to A- retake on a 3-credit course lifts 2.25 quality points - on 90 GPA credits that is 0.025 of CGPA. Decide whether that is worth a full course fee and your scholarship eligibility.

book.text: Standing, probation and leave

rows: CGPA from 1.00 to below 2.25 after your first two semesters, or any later one, puts you on probation for the next two semesters. Reach 2.25 by then or be dismissed. On probation you cannot drop a semester or take leave.
CGPA below 1.00 after the first two or any later semester means automatic dismissal. A dismissed student may apply to another program by passing its admission test.
The academic calendar sets an in-person advising day for students with CGPA 2.15 or less (admitted up to Summer 2023) or 2.40 or less (admitted from Fall 2023), and for everyone on probation.

A student in good standing can take up to three consecutive semesters (one academic year) of leave through the Dean, naming the return semester. Absence without permission is penalised - 20%, 30% or 40% of nine credits' tuition for one, two or three semesters - and beyond three semesters you are withdrawn.
The student rules ask for attendance of not less than 70%-80% of lectures, tutorials and practical classes in each course. Check each course outline for the figure your instructor applies.

Final scripts are not re-evaluated. You can ask for a check of marking or totalling errors for Tk 200 a script (refunded if the error was the faculty member's). Grade changes must reach the Controller of Examinations within seven days of the next semester.

Zero tolerance for copying, unauthorised help and other unfair means; cases go to the Dean. EWU also publishes a Plagiarism Policy and an Artificial Intelligence Policy (ewubd.edu/ewu-policies) - read both before you submit work made with any tool.

book.text: Sources: EWU 'Grades, Rules and Regulations', 'Rules & Regulation' and Fall 2026 academic calendar pages.

book.text: the Toolkit tab - The B.Pharm toolkit
Pharmacy is a memory course, a calculation course and a laboratory course at the same time. Eight tools, one for each way you are examined - and for the industry that is watching.
1. Semester one: do this first

book.text: The semester picture

B.Pharm runs two semesters a year, so a four-year plan has eight. The published course codes run PHRM 101-103, 201-211, 301-312 and 401-414. Copy your own semester-by-semester list from your advising sheet into the Degree tab, then mark here which semesters carry your heaviest loads.
2. Drug cards
Pharmacology (PHRM 301, 306 and 413) rewards students who build their own cards drug class by drug class and revise them on a schedule. One card per prototype drug; one line per class member.

3. Structure sheets for medicinal chemistry
For PHRM 302, 304 and 412, learn each drug class as a skeleton plus the changes that matter. If you can draw the core and annotate it, you can answer most questions on it.

book.text: Instrument cards

The department's lab page lists HPLC, UV-Visible spectrophotometer, FTIR, gas chromatography, dissolution apparatus, ELISA, a PCR thermocycler and a freeze dryer among its equipment. Make a card for each one you use.
The 'Pharma Calc' sheet under Logs and calculators in the Toolkit tab does dilution, percent-of-label-claim and simple dose-volume arithmetic so you can check your hand working.
6. Practical classes and viva

rows: Read the experiment. Write the principle in two lines and the calculation you will need. List the glassware and reagents.

Be able to state the principle, the role of each reagent, the limits, and what you would do if the result failed.

The chairperson's page lists industry-linked in-plant training, industrial visits and sessions with industry professionals as part of the program. Treat every hour in a plant as interview preparation.

PHRM 404 Pharmaceutical Research and your project work go better when the topic is close to what a faculty member already does. The department lists research areas including:

book.title: Professional registration
items: Pharmacy practice in Bangladesh is regulated by the Pharmacy Council of Bangladesh (PCB). EWU requires newly admitted B.Pharm students to complete online pre-registration with the PCB, through the department, within the first three months of their first semester - if you are new, do this first.
The steps from graduation to registration as a pharmacist are set by the PCB and have changed over the years. Ask the department office and check the Council's current notices in your final year.
